{{Quote|Tangle guns were mothballed some time back when Imperial policy moved from one of seduction to one of brute force.|Airen Cracken, ''Cracken's Rebel Field Guide''|<ref name="CRFG" />}}
The '''Anti-Riot Tangle Gun 7''', also known as the '''tangle pistol''', was a crowd-control defense weapon manufactured by [[Merr-Sonn Munitions, Inc./Legends|Merr-Sonn Munitions]] for the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], though it eventually became available on the [[Black market/Legends|black market]] in the [[Ringali Shell]] region of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]. The [[tangle gun]] fired a [[Pellet/Legends|pellet]] that, when exposed to [[Atmosphere/Legends|air]], explosively expanded into a multi&ndash;[[Meter/Legends|meter]]&ndash;wide webbed [[Net/Legends|net]] that enveloped its victim and then shrank, thus immobilizing the target. The webbing sometimes contracted too tightly, causing the victim to suffocate and [[Death/Legends|die]]. [[General/Legends|General]] [[Airen Cracken/Legends|Airen Cracken]] included an entry for the weapon in his [[Cracken's Rebel Field Guide|field guide]] for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]].

==Description==
{{Quote|The fact that they were supposed to be non-lethal weapons does not mean that they cannot kill. Despite efforts by Merr-Sonn, the tangle webs often contract too much, doing serious damage to the trapped person.|Airen Cracken, ''Cracken's Rebel Field Guide''|<ref name="CRFG" />}}
[[File:AntiRiotTangleGun7-CRFG.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The tangle gun used a naorstrachem pellet that exploded into a web, trapping its target.]]
The Anti-Riot Tangle Gun 7,<ref name="CRFG" /> sometimes referred to simply as the tangle [[Pistol/Legends|pistol]],<ref name="AED" /> was a crowd-control defense weapon that shot a [[Naorstrachem/Legends|naorstrachem]] [[Pellet/Legends|pellet]] mixed with a shrinking agent. When exposed to [[Atmosphere/Legends|air]], the pellet explosively expanded into a webbed [[Net/Legends|net]] several [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in width. The net automatically contracted as soon as it came into contact with a [[Temperature/Legends|warm]] surface, such as a living body. It then wrapped around the target and tightened, trapping the target almost instantly. However, a problem with [[tangle gun]]s like the Tangle Gun 7 was that the webbing often contracted too much, resulting in the target being suffocated&mdash;and sometimes [[Death/Legends|killed]]&mdash;by the intense pressure of the webbing.<ref name="CRFG" />

The tangle gun carried a load of fifteen pellets and had a short range of three-to-ten meters, a medium range of eleven-to-nineteen meters, and a long range of twenty-to-twenty-five meters.<ref name="CRFG" /> The size of a [[Blaster carbine/Legends|blaster carbine]] and lightweight, the tangle gun had a light [[Polycarbonate/Legends|polycarbonate]] furniture and a short, wide-mouthed [[Barrel/Legends|barrel]].<ref name="FH" /> The tangle gun was also composed of an additional [[Polymer/Legends|polymer]] material, non-ferrous metal, and [[Codoran|Codoan Copper]].<ref name="AED" /> The reload cartridge of the tangle gun was located at the top rear just above the handle. Regularly priced at 300<ref name="CRFG" />&ndash;to&ndash;500 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]],<ref name="FH" /> the weapon was considered a specialized item that was not available everywhere and was even considered to be illegal on most [[Planet/Legends|planets]].<ref name="GFT">''[[Galladinium's Fantastic Technology]]''</ref>

==History==
[[File:TanglePistol.png|thumb|right|300px|A tangle pistol]]
The tangle gun was produced by [[Merr-Sonn Munitions, Inc./Legends|Merr-Sonn Munitions, Inc.]] for use by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]],<ref name="CRFG" /> though schematics of the weapon were also available to independent [[weaponsmith]]s and [[Merchant/Legends|munitions traders]].<ref name="AED" /> Manufactured to meet the Empire's need for a more humane crowd-control weapon than a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]], the Anti-Riot Tangle Gun 7 was often used when non-lethal force was needed. However, once Imperial policy adopted a more brutal approach, the Empire ceased using the weapon.<ref name="CRFG" />

During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], [[General/Legends|General]] [[Airen Cracken/Legends|Airen Cracken]] included the tangle gun in ''[[Cracken's Rebel Field Guide]]'', a report he authored for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] documenting various Imperial munitions. The field guide's section on the tangle gun featured an illustration of the weapon, along with a depiction of a [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] caught in the gun's webbing.<ref name="CRFG" /> The tangle gun was also listed in the [[Galladinium's 50th anniversary edition|fiftieth-anniversary issue]] of ''[[Galladinium's Galactic Datalog of Fantastic Technology]]'', which purveyed fine merchandise to an upscale clientele during the war. The [[Datalog/Legends|datalog]] listed the tangle gun at a price of 300 credits.<ref name="GFT" />

In the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]],<ref name="Date">''[[The Far Orbit Project]]'' dates the [[EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate/Legends|starship]] ''[[Far Orbit]]''{{'s}} campaign within a few [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]] after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], which corresponds to the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], according to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.</ref> during the missions of the [[Privateer/Legends|privateer]] [[EF76 Nebulon-B escort frigate/Legends|starship]] ''[[Far Orbit]]'' in the [[Ringali Shell]] area of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]], the tangle gun was available on that region's [[Black market/Legends|black market]]. It started off at a price of 300 credits but jumped to 6,000 credits once the Empire became aware of the ''Far Orbit''{{'s}} activities. The privateer [[Starship/Legends|vessel]] retreated from the Ringali Shell following a [[Battle in Brentaal space|defeat]] against [[Imperial Military|Imperial forces]]; upon the ship's return sometime later, the tangle gun's black-market value had risen to 9,000 credits.<ref name="TFOP" />

{{RPG|"[[The Farrimmer Cafe]]"}}
Some [[Time/Legends|time]] during the Galactic Civil War, an Anti-Riot Tangle Gun 7 was concealed in a hidden compartment in a chair at the [[Farrimmer Cafe]], an [[Restaurant/Legends|eatery]] on the [[Mynock 7 Space Station]]. The [[Filvian]] owner, [[H'nib Statermast]], was unaware of the compartment and the pistol, which were discovered by a group of individuals as they searched the restaurant for one of several [[Bomb/Legends|bombs]] that had been suspected of being placed throughout the [[Space station/Legends|space station]]. Statermast was not concerned with whether or not the individuals kept the pistol and any other items they discovered during their search.<ref name="TFC">{{JournalCite|11|The Farrimmer Cafe}}</ref>
{{Endgame}}

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Crackensrebelfieldguide.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The tangle gun was introduced in ''Cracken's Rebel Field Guide''.]]
The Anti-Riot Tangle Gun 7 was introduced in [[Cracken's Rebel Field Guide (sourcebook)|''Cracken's Rebel Field Guide'']], a [[1991]] sourcebook written by [[Christopher Kubasik]] for [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="CRFG" /> The weapon first appeared in "[[The Farrimmer Cafe]]," a set of [[roleplaying game]] adventures published in the [[1996]] [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 11|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 11]] and written by [[Jean Rabe]] and [[J. Allan Fawcett]]. In one of the adventures, the tangle gun can be discovered by the player characters if they agree to search the Farrimmer Cafe on H'nib Statermast's behalf and then successfully perform a roll of a "Heroic" difficulty while inspecting the establishment's tables.<ref name="TFC" /> The weapon appeared in the [[2003]] [[LucasArts]]&ndash;[[Sony]] Online Entertainment [[Star Wars video games|MMORPG]] [[Star Wars Galaxies|''Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided'']],<ref name="AED" /> prior to its closure in [[2011]].<ref name="Shutdown">{{SonyCite|url=playerinfo|text=IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT ''STAR WARS'' GALAXIES™}}</ref> In the game, the [[W:c:swg:Weapon|weapon]] was simply identified as a "[[W:c:swg:Tangle Pistol|tangle pistol]]," and it could be [[W:c:swg:Crafting|crafted]] by [[W:c:swg:Weaponsmith (pre NGE)|weaponsmiths]] and later by [[W:c:swg:Trader (Munitions)|munitions traders]] using a number of different [[W:c:swg:Ranged weapon component|components]] and [[W:c:swg:Resource|resources]], including [[W:c:swg:Codoan copper|Codoan Copper]], [[W:c:swg:Non-ferrous metal|non-ferrous metal]], and [[W:c:swg:Polymer|polymer]].<ref name="AED" />

Various ''Star Wars Galaxies'' reference guides provide differing statistics for the tangle gun. ''[[Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided: Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]'' (2003), ''[[Star Wars Galaxies: Jump to Lightspeed: Prima Official Game Guide]]'' ([[2004]]), and ''[[Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided Quick Reference Guide]]'' (2004) identify the tangle gun as a [[Stun/Legends|stun]] weapon with a maximum range of forty-eight meters,<ref name="Prima">[[Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]</ref><ref name="QuickRef">''[[Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided Quick Reference Guide]]''</ref><ref name="JTL">[[Star Wars Galaxies: Jump to Lightspeed: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars Galaxies: Jump to Lightspeed'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref> while ''[[Star Wars Galaxies: The Total Experience: Prima Official Game Guide]]'' and ''[[Star Wars Galaxies: The Complete Guide: Prima Official Game Guide]]'' ([[2005]]) identify it as a [[W:c:swg:Kinetic damage|kinetic]] weapon with a range of thirty-five meters,<ref name="Total">[[Star Wars Galaxies: The Total Experience: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars Galaxies: The Total Experience'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref><ref name="Complete">[[Star Wars Galaxies: The Complete Guide: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars Galaxies: The Complete Guide'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref> reflecting the [[W:c:swg:Combat Upgrade|gameplay overhaul]] in 2005.<ref name="CU">{{SonyCite|url=content.jsp?page=Combat%20Upgrade:%20Core%20Combat%20Changes|text=Combat Upgrade: Core Combat Changes}}</ref>  Given the ambiguity of these statistics, this article uses the twenty-five-meter figure provided in ''Cracken's Rebel Field Guide''.<ref name="CRFG" /> In another inconsistency, the [[Fantasy Flight Games]] ''[[Star Wars: Edge of the Empire]]'' sourcebook ''[[Far Horizons]]'', which was released in [[2014]], refers to the tangle gun as a [[Rifle/Legends|rifle]].<ref name="FH" />
